headline: Lawrence mayor indicted on wiretap and witness-intimidation charges
dek: A statewide grand jury returned 15 indictments against Brian DePeña over alleged secret recordings at City Hall; his arraignment has not been scheduled.
body: A Massachusetts statewide grand jury has indicted Lawrence Mayor Brian DePeña on 15 charges tied to alleged secret recordings made inside City Hall, Attorney General Andrea Campbell's office announced Thursday. The indictment includes 14 counts of distributing a wiretapped communication and one count of witness intimidation.

According to the attorney general's office, DePeña requested and installed a private security system for his office in 2023, separate from the city's existing cameras. In March, one of those cameras allegedly recorded audio and video of a hallway conversation between two public employees, at least one of whom did not know the conversation was being recorded.

Prosecutors allege that DePeña later distributed copies of the recording to 14 people. The attorney general's office said the city's own security cameras do not record audio and that there was no public notice that the mayor's private system captured sound. Massachusetts State Police and Lawrence police assisted with the investigation, according to the office.

The arraignment on the state charges will be scheduled later. The case is separate from federal charges filed in August alleging that DePeña obtained more than $1.5 million in pandemic-era small-business loans and used some of the money for personal expenses and his mayoral campaign. DePeña has pleaded not guilty to those federal charges, according to court coverage. The new indictment contains allegations, not findings of guilt.
author: NorthEast News Desk
